summary: External HR survey link triggered creation of privileged GitHub webhook subscriptions
description:
Issue summary: An employee opened an external HR survey email and followed a link. Within 30 minutes we observed a new GitHub webhook subscription created against the private repo 'infra/ops' with elevated event scopes (pull_request, push, repository). Impact: The webhook secret was briefly visible in audit logs and the webhook delivered two requests to an external endpoint before we removed it. No confirmed data exfiltration yet, but the webhook could have forwarded CI event payloads containing commit metadata and repo references. Environment: Production GitHub org, infra repositories, affected users are internal engineering accounts.

Observed evidence: 1) GitHub audit entry at 2026-03-10T14:07:12Z shows 'webhook.created' by user akumar@redwood.com from IP 52.205.14.213. 2) The webhook URL pointed to a third-party domainsurvey[.]io endpoint. 3) At 14:08 and 14:12 we see two webhook deliveries with 200 responses from that endpoint. 4) Internal Access logs show user opened external survey URL from same workstation at 13:58.

Initial hypothesis: The external HR survey contained a scripted form that prompted an OAuth/GitHub authorization flow or an embedded token-exchange that allowed creation of webhooks via the employee's session or a stored PAT. Alternate hypothesis: A browser extension injected by the survey page triggered GitHub API calls using cached credentials.

Business impact: Potential exposure of metadata and CI signals. Risk of token theft or subsequent automated actions if webhook target received payloads with secrets (unlikely but must be verified).

Immediate ask: Security and SRE to rotate webhook secrets, revoke any tokens created from timeframe, collect full audit timeline, and identify other similar webhook creations across org. Request for Legal/Privacy to evaluate data contained in delivered payloads and decide on disclosure if PII is present.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Employee receives external HR survey email (sent from hr-survey@vendor-example.com)
2) Employee clicks 'Complete survey' which opens external domainsurvey[.]io with embedded script
3) Script opens a new tab to github.com/login?return_to=/settings/apps or executes a REST call to api.github.com/repos/infra/ops/hooks with Authorization header if extension/session available
4) Observe new webhook created and deliveries to domainsurvey[.]io
5) If reproduced, capture full request/response including headers and webhook payload bodies for analysis

2026-03-10T14:15:00Z - security - webhooks - secret_rotation - initiated by: lena.park@redwood.com
investigation_notes: 14:20 - SRE: Rotated webhook secret and deleted hook_id 987654. Confirmed no additional deliveries after deletion.
15:05 - Security: Requested full payloads from domainsurvey.io via takedown/abuse contact; vendor reports they store payloads for 30 days.
15:30 - Identity: Checked recent token issuance for akumar@redwood.com; found no new PATs or OAuth apps created in the same window, but browser extension API access could not be ruled out.
16:10 - SRE: Scanned org for webhooks created between 2026-03-09 and 2026-03-11; found 3 additional webhooks with external endpoints created by non-admins — all removed and owners contacted.
17:00 - Security: Noted the IP 52.205.14.213 resolves to a cloud hosting provider in eu-west; additional telemetry shows similar IP in historical spam activity lists.
18:00 - Action item: Request for endpoint team to check device of reporter for malicious browser extensions and run YARA/AV scan.
comments: Marcus Nguyen (Reporter) - 2026-03-10 14:25: I clicked the survey link while at my desk. I did not enter any GitHub credentials; Chrome may have used existing session cookies. I noticed a redirect to a page that said 'Connect to GitHub to continue' but I did not explicitly click 'Authorize'.

Lena Park (Assignee, SRE) - 2026-03-10 14:40: Rotated webhook secret and deleted hook_id 987654. Asking Security to pull payload bodies and check for sensitive fields. Also scanning org for similar hooks now.

Priya Shah (Security) - 2026-03-10 15:10: We called the domainsurvey abuse contact; they confirmed receipt of two deliveries and are preserving logs. We've requested full JSON bodies and source IPs. If payloads contain PII/credentials we'll escalate to Legal.

On-call Infra (Slack #oncall-sre) - 2026-03-10 15:50: Found two more external hooks created 2026-03-09 22:14 and 2026-03-10 03:33 by different developers. Both removed and owners notified. We're rolling a policy change proposal to restrict webhook creation to org-admins pending further review.
Marcus Nguyen - 2026-03-10 16:05: I ran an extension audit; I have 'SurveyHelper' extension installed which I did not recall adding. I have disabled it and submitted it to IT for removal.

Security (Priya Shah) - 2026-03-11 09:00: Endpoint team completed AV scan on Marcus's machine; no malware found but the extension had permissions to read and modify pages. Suggest org-wide extension telemetry and a blocker policy for high-risk extensions.

Lena Park - 2026-03-11 12:30: Created temporary enforcement: only org-admins and CI agents can create webhooks. Implemented a pre-commit webhook creation policy on GitHub via organization settings. Need product approvals to make permanent.
resolution: Mitigations implemented: removed malicious webhooks, rotated secrets, revoked no tokens found, removed suspicious browser extension on reporter device, temporary policy to restrict webhook creation to admins. Next steps: Security to obtain delivery payloads and Legal to review; Product to approve permanent webhook policy. Post-incident: run org-wide extension telemetry and user training on external links.
